note: Twig Xdebug is a thin wrapper that registers the ajgl/breakpoint-twig-extension library as a Twig extension (service id 'twig_xdebug' -> class Ajgl\Twig\Extension\BreakpointExtension, tagged twig.extension). It adds a single Twig function breakpoint(); rendering {{ breakpoint() }} calls PHP xdebug_break(). It has NO config, routes, permissions, schema, or plugins, so introspection/execution cases are grounded in the module's only real artifact: Twig templates that call breakpoint(). Medium cases read back which variable/expression a template passes to breakpoint(); hard cases require authoring a template that sets a breakpoint (on `node`, or argument-less). Template files live under the site files dir so they are inspectable and verifiable without touching shared site config.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the twig_xdebug module enabled, how do I set an Xdebug breakpoint inside a Twig template, and what underlying PHP function does that trigger?
evals.expected_output: Write {{ breakpoint() }} (optionally {{ breakpoint(someVar) }}) in the Twig template. When Twig renders it, the ajgl/breakpoint-twig-extension Twig extension calls PHP's xdebug_break(), pausing execution in your IDE with the template's variables in scope.

evals.prompt: What Composer library does the Drupal twig_xdebug module depend on, and what does the module register in the service container to expose its Twig function?
evals.expected_output: It requires ajgl/breakpoint-twig-extension (^0.3.4). The module registers a service 'twig_xdebug' whose class is Ajgl\Twig\Extension\BreakpointExtension, tagged with twig.extension, which provides the breakpoint() Twig function.

evals.prompt: In a Twig template using twig_xdebug, how do I focus the debugger on one specific value, and what variables are available at the breakpoint?
evals.expected_output: Pass the value as an argument, e.g. {{ breakpoint(fields) }}; it appears as $arguments at the breakpoint. Also available are $context (all template variables) and $environment (the Twig environment). Execution pauses inside the library's BreakpointExtension.php.

evals.prompt: On this site there is a Twig template at web/sites/default/files/tx_med1/report.html.twig that uses twig_xdebug to set a breakpoint. Inspect the template and state which variable is being passed to breakpoint() for inspection.
evals.expected_output: The template calls {{ breakpoint(items) }}, so the variable being inspected at the breakpoint is `items`.

evals.prompt: A Twig template at web/sites/default/files/tx_med2/body.html.twig on this site sets a twig_xdebug breakpoint. Inspect it and report the exact expression passed to breakpoint().
evals.expected_output: The template calls {{ breakpoint(node.field_body.value) }}, so the expression passed to the breakpoint is node.field_body.value.

evals.prompt: Using the twig_xdebug module, create a Twig template file at web/sites/default/files/tx_hard1/debug.html.twig that sets an Xdebug breakpoint which inspects the `node` variable when the template renders.
evals.expected_output: Create the file containing {{ breakpoint(node) }} (twig_xdebug's breakpoint() Twig function with `node` as the argument), which calls xdebug_break() and lets you inspect `node` at that point.

evals.prompt: I have the twig_xdebug module on. I want my debugger to stop while a template is drawing so I can see every variable the template got. Create the file web/sites/default/files/tx_hard2/inspect.html.twig that makes that happen (with no particular variable singled out).
evals.expected_output: Create the file containing an argument-less {{ breakpoint() }}; when the template renders, twig_xdebug calls xdebug_break() and the whole Twig $context (all template variables) is inspectable in the debugger.
